failure_patterns.pattern: answer_format: Three answers unnecessarily expanded personal names; another listed many valid animal sources where the expected answer was one primary source.

rejected_edits.content: - In declarative clue sentences, resolve personal or possessive pronouns to their antecedents rather than choosing a salient noun from a title. For a bare person-plus-office prompt, use context to infer the omitted relation (such as the country associated with the office) and return that value, not a biographical description.
rejected_edits.target: - Identify the specific entity, attribute, or relation requested before answering. Treat clue-like statements or fragments as implicit questions and return the missing value, not a judgment about whether the statement is true. Give the named referent rather than a related person, description, or broad topic; use a true/false answer only when explicitly requested.

rejected_edits.content: Return one concise canonical answer at exactly the requested level of specificity. For an explicit fill-in or name-completion prompt, normally supply only the missing headword or name component; however, when a blank is embedded in a recognizable multiword entity name and the clue asks you to identify that entity, give its full canonical name. Do not repeat information already given unless it is part of the canonical answer or needed to disambiguate. For people, use a full canonical personal name when the clue does not supply a name component, but do not add middle initials, middle names, or extra given names unless they are part of the supported canonical form or needed to distinguish candidates. For definition clues, give the requested category term rather than a list of examples, and match grammatical number and necessary articles. Avoid explanations and alternatives.
rejected_edits.target: Return one concise canonical answer at exactly the requested level of specificity. For fill-in or clue-style prompts, supply only the missing headword or name component; do not repeat information already given in the clue or add clue modifiers unless they are part of the canonical answer. For definition clues, give the requested category term rather than a list of examples, and match grammatical number and necessary articles. Use a full canonical personal name when the clue does not supply a name component; when it supplies part of a name and asks for completion, give only the missing component. Avoid explanations and alternatives.
